clue.text: Secretary — person with importance that tops the pile?

parts.note: a personal assistant, a PA, does secretarial work
PER is a short form of person, as in the abbreviation pers.
weight means influence or significance

explanation.surface: An office secretary is cast as a figure of real consequence, sitting at the top of the heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops the pile' sounds like being the boss, but it is literal: the thing sitting on top of a stack of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy desk object placed on loose sheets to hold them down, so it literally sits atop the stack.

clue.text: New Father Ted plot curtly condemned as child's work

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are knocked into a new order
said curtly, the word plot is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A new storyline for the sitcom Father Ted is dismissed as something a child could have written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtly' trims PLOT to PLO; 'condemned' rearranges NEW FATHER TED PLO. Father Ted is a British-Irish TV sitcom about priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's musical tale is a famous composition written to introduce children to orchestral instruments.

clue.text: Authentic sound coming from cockle

indicators.note: the word pucker is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to cockle is to wrinkle or pucker, as paper does when damp

explanation.surface: Seems to claim a genuine noise issuing from a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockle' looks like the shellfish, but here it is the verb meaning to crease or wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine or first-class, the real thing.

clue.text: Novelist's career to come to an end

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
to die is to stop or expire

explanation.surface: A writer's working life is about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for a working life, but it is the verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is the author of Midnight's Children and The Satanic Verses.

clue.text: Chilled dessert served up after rest

indicators.note: after places the rest word in front of the dessert part

parts.note: ease means rest or relaxation

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up has the word for dessert read from bottom to top

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a British word for dessert

explanation.surface: A cold pudding is brought out after a break in the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reads the dessert word bottom to top in this down entry. 'Chilled' looks like a cold dessert, but means relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying someone has relaxed or slackened off.

clue.text: Grouse, maybe, as valiant effort restricts runs

parts.note: game means plucky or willing

indicators.note: restricts means holds in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or effort
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A brave attempt is hampered by the batting side's runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricts' puts R inside BID to give BIRD. 'Grouse' looks like a complaint, but it is the moorland bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is an example of a wild bird shot for sport.

clue.text: Eponymous man of Nazareth appearing randomly in records

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for records

parts.note: tapes are recordings

indicators.note: randomly means the letters fall in no set order

explanation.surface: A figure from Nazareth turns up here and there in archives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' turns OF NAZARETH into ARZANOFTHE, which goes 'in' TAPES. 'man of Nazareth' suggests Jesus, but only 'of Nazareth' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Burroughs' novel is named after its ape-raised hero, so the title character is its eponymous man.

clue.text: Criminal deferring pint, impressed by police?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker, putting off a drink, gets taken in by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges DEFERRING PINT. 'impressed' is used literally: prints are pressed in ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Police take ink impressions of a suspect's fingertips when booking them.

clue.text: In office, reasonably well placed

parts.note: a sitting member is one currently holding office
pretty means fairly or reasonably, as in pretty good

explanation.surface: Someone currently in post is fairly comfortably positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a comfortable, advantageous position.

clue.text: New classes seeing how films are recorded

definitions.meaning: batches of new pupils or recruits
films are shot ..., so they are recorded ...

explanation.surface: Fresh students learning the way movies are shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's yearly intake is its new enrolment; split, the word also describes shooting a film take by take.

clue.text: Drive back suspect, like top-class fighter of old

indicators.note: to drive something back is to turn it round, so these words are read from the end

parts.note: rum means odd or suspect
as means like
A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: An order to repel a dubious, first-rate warrior from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive back' reverses RUMAS to SAMUR. 'Drive' looks like an order to steer, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Freshly crowned leaders of Greece and Rome put down

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

parts.note: landed means set down or brought to earth

explanation.surface: The heads of two ancient powers, newly crowned, are deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes G, A, R from Greece, and, Rome. 'put down' looks like a deposition, but just means landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being garlanded means having a wreath of flowers placed on one's head.

clue.text: Little devil that's caught cutting part of plant

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A naughty child is caught snipping a bit of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like taking a plant cutting, but it puts C inside BRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf at the base of a flower, as in poinsettia.

clue.text: See 14
Cereal crop cut at end of season for nominal fee

indicators.note: at end of puts the crop and cut pieces after the season word

parts.note: to pepper food is to season it
corn is a cereal crop
rent means torn or cut

explanation.surface: A grain harvest is cut short as the season closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' looks like a time of year, but it is the verb meaning to spice.
explanation.definitionFit: A token rent, traditionally a single peppercorn, paid to keep a lease legally valid.

clue.text: Cyclist skirting large metropolis, Rome perhaps

indicators.note: skirting means going around the edge, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track cyclist
a metropolis is a city

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides round the edge of a great city like Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Hoy is a Scottish Olympic cycling champion; 'skirting' puts his name around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is called a sacred city as seat of the papacy, as are Jerusalem and Mecca.

clue.text: Great sport with deer — sadly it'll set you back a bit

definitions.text: it'll set you back a bit

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Hunting deer as a great sport is lamented as a backward move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges GREAT SPORT DEER. 'set you back' sounds like a cost, but here means a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A move that worsens a situation is a backward move, putting progress back somewhat.

clue.text: One state's revolutionary broadcast blocked by another

indicators.note: blocked by means stopped up by something placed inside
revolutionary means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
another state, Oman in Arabia

explanation.surface: One country's rebel radio station is jammed by a neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns AIR into RIA, which OMAN fills. 'revolutionary' looks political, but means turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country of south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: First to last, benefit in backing police is hard to fathom

indicators.note: in places the benefit piece inside the police piece
backing means going in reverse, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: First to last moves the opening letter to the end

parts.note: to help is to benefit

explanation.surface: Supporting the police turns out to be a puzzling benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to last' makes HELP into ELPH, which goes 'in' DIC ('backing' CID).
explanation.definitionFit: The Delphic oracle gave notoriously ambiguous answers, so the word means obscure or enigmatic.

clue.text: See 16
Poor journalist longing to get back outside

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the journalist goes within
to get back means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a craving or longing
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An impoverished reporter yearns to return home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' turns YEN into NEY, which goes 'outside' ED.
explanation.definitionFit: The needy are those lacking money or necessities, the hard-up.

clue.text: Muse as setter consumes exotic lemon pie I overlooked

indicators.note: consumes means eats up, so the setter word holds the rest

parts.note: a crossword setter refers to themself as ME

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and unusual, so the letters are rearranged
overlooked means left out, so the I is dropped

explanation.surface: A muse-like setter eats an unusual lemon pie, ignoring something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the I that is 'overlooked' leaves LEMONPE; 'exotic' rearranges it to ELPOMEN, which ME 'consumes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene is the Muse of tragedy, one of the nine Muses of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Bizarre public reaction, battle being lost

parts.note: out means in the open, publicly known

indicators.note: being lost means that part is dropped

parts.note: an action is a military engagement

explanation.surface: Odd public response when a battle is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public reaction' reads as one phrase but splits in two; 'being lost' takes the battle word out of reaction, leaving just its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means unconventional or eccentric.

clue.text: Eg Boris's message rejected by Scotsman

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a note is a short message
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A note from Boris is turned down by a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson went to Eton, the elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson is an example of a former pupil of Eton College.

clue.text: Good place for reception where trouble may flare up?

definitions.meaning: a wifi access point gives good signal reception
a trouble spot liable to break into violence

explanation.surface: Pleasant place for a party, but things may turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both a public wireless access point and a place of conflict or danger.

clue.text: Slips in field, perhaps, chasing cunning wingers

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the fielders follow the cunning word

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or cunning
in cricket, slips are fielders placed to catch edges, so catchers

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders chase clever wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Slips are cricket fielders beside the wicketkeeper. 'wingers' suggests football wide men, but means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Flycatchers are small birds that snatch insects in flight, so winged creatures.
